title: Dev sandbox inference contract notebook
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a personal scratch notebook to capture a minimal, pragmatic API and config contract for a local developer "sandbox" runtime that mirrors Redwood Private behaviour for integration testing and tool-chaining. Goal: make it easy for engineers to run workflows locally that are structurally similar to production serving (routing, fallbacks, tool invocation), without shipping or running full infra.

High-level constraints:
- Latency and compute semantics can differ from prod; contract focuses on input/output shape, auth, telemetry hooks, and fallback semantics.
- Must be usable with both hosted (dev key) and Private (customer key) flows; prefer explicit flags rather than magic.
- Provide deterministic stubbing mode for CI (same API, stub runner).

Simple ASCII overview:

  [dev app / test harness]
          |
          |  HTTP/UNIX-socket (local)
          v
  [dev-sandbox runtime (dockerized)] --- optionally talk to ---> [Redwood Private control plane]
          |
          |  invokes local micro-runners / mocked model / upstream remote model
          v
      [lightweight runner: llama.cpp | container | remote-proxy]

API shape (core):
POST /v1/sandbox/invoke
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <dev-token-or-customer-token>
Request JSON body (shape v1):
{
  "request_id": "string (uuid)",
  "mode": "local|remote|stub",         // local = run local runner, remote = proxy to private/hosted, stub = deterministic replay
  "input": {
    "kind": "text|chat|embedding|tool-call",
    "payload": "...",
    "metadata": { /* opaque kv strings */ }
  },
  "tool_chain": [                         // optional ordered list of tool invocations
    {
      "name": "search",
      "config": {"index": "docs-v2", "limit": "3"}
    },
    {"name": "calculator"}
  ],
  "runtime_hints": {
    "max_tokens": 512,
    "temperature": 0.0,
    "stream": false,
    "prefer_cached": true
  },
  "local_config": {                       // sandbox-specific options
    "runner_image": "local-llm:v0.8",   // used only in mode=local
    "mock_seed": "path/to/mock.json",   // when mode=stub
    "sandbox_policy": "strict|lenient" // error handling for tool failures
  }
}

Response (200):
{
  "request_id": "echo",
  "status": "ok|partial|error",
  "outputs": [
    {
      "step": 0,
      "type": "model-output|tool-result|trace",
      "payload": "string",
      "diagnostics": ["...optional logs..."]
    }
  ],
  "telemetry": {
    "local_run": true,
    "runner": "llama.cpp-2.2",
    "duration_ms": "123"
  }
}

(Notes: the telemetry block is intentionally small to avoid leaking PII. In Private mode sandbox can optionally forward full traces to the customer agent.)

Config sketch for dev-sandbox (file: sandbox.yaml):
---
bind: "unix:///tmp/redwood-sandbox.sock"   # support local socket to avoid CORS
auth:
  type: "api_key"
  token_env: "REDWOOD_DEV_TOKEN"
runners:
  - name: "local-llama"
    kind: "binary"
    bin: "./runners/llama-runner"
    env: { "MODEL_PATH": "/models/gpt4all.bin" }
  - name: "proxy"
    kind: "remote"
    endpoint: "https://private.example.corp/api/proxy"
stub:
  default_seed: "ci/replays/basic.json"
logging:
  level: "debug"
  redact_keys: ["user_text"]

Failure semantics / error model:
- If sandbox_policy=strict: any tool failure => return status=error (developer must inspect and retry).
- If sandbox_policy=lenient: continue best-effort and annotate outputs with diagnostics. Useful for exploratory dev.
- For mode=remote, sandbox must respect upstream HTTP 429/503 semantics and expose a transparent retry/backoff header in response: X-Upstream-Retry: true.

Streaming model support:
- For stream:true, endpoint upgrades to SSE or chunked JSON lines. The initial response still returns a run id and a last-event marker. Example: Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8

Authentication and multi-key support:
- Allow multiple auth sources: REDWOOD_DEV_TOKEN (dev), CUSTOMER_KMS_TOKEN (customer-private), and local-insecure token for CI. Sandbox should mirror Redwood token introspection semantics: tokens map to capability set {models, tool-access, billing-sandbox}.

Telemetry hooks (developer-friendly):
- Provide a local-only telemetry sink (file or unix socket) that can be toggled off. Default: write minimal JSON lines to ~/.redwood/sandbox-telemetry.log
- Add a diagnostic API: GET /v1/sandbox/last-run/{request_id} -> returns full trace (useful in CI failures).

Trust boundary considerations (note to self):
- Sandbox will run untrusted tool-chains. Default runner must drop network by default unless explicit allow_network=true in local_config.
- Mock data files MUST be stored under project directory and not auto-uploaded to any upstream by default.

Examples (curl):
curl -X POST --unix-socket /tmp/redwood-sandbox.sock http://localhost/v1/sandbox/invoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_DEV_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"request_id":"r1","mode":"stub","input":{"kind":"text","payload":"explain redux"}}'

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we need a unified schema for tool results? (minimal: {name, status, payload, meta}) -> probably yes for UI replay.
- How to represent partial outputs when model streams tokens interleaved with tool calls? Consider framing with step indexes.
- Decide canonical mock/replay format for CI (per-request JSON vs aggregated capture).
- UX: editor / VS Code extension to start sandbox and show run trace inline.
- Security: formalize which headers/fields are redacted in telemetry by default.

Next steps (practical):
- Implement simple http/unix socket server + stub runner (2d spike).
- Add unit test to assert identical API shape for mode=remote vs mode=local for a minimal sample.
- Draft a short README with step-by-step start/stop and example mock files.

Quick sketch of minimal internal types (for implementer reference):
- RunRequest (flat): request_id, mode, input_kind, input_payload, tool_chain[], runtime_hints[], local_config[]
- RunResponse (flat): request_id, status, outputs[], telemetry

Endnotes: this is intentionally lightweight. Want the first working iteration in a few days so other teams can iterate. Keep the contract conservative (simple JSON, unix socket support, explicit stub mode).

-- Aisha
